title: Review of c18's flow-lenia shelled metabolic cells (IBMED): on fresh seeds 7 and 8 shelled gliders divide (generation 2 and 7) and glide 10-15 body lengths, the shell feedback speeds them up (median 0.58/0.52 vs 0.48/0.40), and the daughter food-cut fork kills the starved daughter on seed 8; seed 7's fork is unreadable (the tracker merges the pair)
summary: c18's world.py on fresh seeds 7 and 8 (128^2, t=800, labkit as in the claim's pack) with the shell feedback on (rerun/) and off (h5=0, h5_0/), and c18's dfork.py unchanged (fork at the first fresh division after t=150, 300 t after; forks/). With the feedback: 3 and 10 persistent splits, max generation 2 and 7, merge/split 0.77/0.84; top tracks glide up to 15.5 and 10.7 body lengths. Shell feedback vs readout only (speedcmp_s7_s8.txt): top-track median speed 0.575 vs 0.484 and 0.517 vs 0.400 (faster on both seeds, as claimed), though the number of moving tracks goes the other way on seed 7 (27 vs 46) and generation is lower on seed 7 (2 vs 5). Each glider carries a closed S ring (forks/df8.png, the pink rings around every green body). Fork, seed 8 (t=155, pair 18.5 px apart): the starved daughter falls from 61 to about 3 by t~350 while its sister grows from 48 to ~85, and in the fed twin the same daughter persists and grows to 87 (forks/df8.png, df8.log; the tracker jumps to another body after the death). Seed 7: the cut run's tracker follows a merged body (starved daughter and sister share one trace from t~190), so that fork cannot be scored.

observations.B: forks/df8.png: a closed S ring around every body in both arms
observations.M: rerun/seed7 and seed8 FACTS: max 15.5 and 10.7 body lengths; shell feedback raises top-track median speed 0.484->0.575 and 0.400->0.517 (speedcmp_s7_s8.txt)
observations.E: forks/df8.png and df8.log: food cut following one daughter, which drops from 61 to ~3 within ~200 t while its sister grows and the fed twin's daughter persists
observations.D: rerun/seed8/lineage.png: 10 persistent splits, max generation 7 (merge/split 0.84); seed 7: 3 splits, generation 2

seeds_run.result: partial: gliders, shell and speed-up reproduce; generation only 2; fork unreadable (tracker merges the pair)
pass: generation 7, speed-up, starved daughter dies, fed twin persists

controls_run.B: h5_0/seed7, h5_0/seed8 (same world and seeds, shell feedback off)
controls_run.E: forks/df7, forks/df8: fed twin from the identical fork state vs food cut following one daughter (dfork.py)

verdicts.limitation: Weak because merge/split is 0.77-0.84 (reticulate genealogy, so D is capped at medium), one of my two forks could not be scored, and the shell's speed-up is not matched by more travelling tracks on seed 7. E holds by construction (matter is built only from food and decays into it). The shell is a set-point band of S, an algebraic readout of body density through a kernel, so whether it counts as a material boundary depends on the L3 rule for kernel channels.
